detail.statement: Autonomous problem significance can be effectively proxied by computational novelty and cascading dependency density in multi-file software environments, though this must be balanced against metrics for analytical curiosity and inquiring mindsets.
detail.reason: New evidence from physics education frameworks confirms that addressing fundamental laws and fostering analytical curiosity provides a necessary qualitative counterpart to purely quantitative code complexity metrics.

detail.title: Obedience-Driven Failures in Autonomous Systems
detail.summary: Autonomous systems relying solely on rigid operator instructions face significant performance and safety risks when encountering non-stationary environments. Effective autonomous agents require self-healing mechanisms and the capacity for self-generated goals to circumvent the failures associated with strict adherence to incomplete or narrow human-provided objectives.
detail.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding rigid vs. autonomous goal setting to address project-specific questions on obedience-driven failures.

detail.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation via Hybrid Architectures and Goal Generation
detail.summary: Integrating computational dependency analysis with structured frameworks of curiosity and fundamental law exploration reveals that automated discovery systems must balance structural complexity metrics with qualitative pedagogical insights to evaluate true problem significance.
detail.reason: Updated with new evidence regarding physics outreach and fundamental law comprehension to strengthen the qualitative basis of autonomous problem significance.
